borrowed_shapes.core_idea: Split into semi-autonomous units by product, geography, or market, each with its own accountability; the center sets direction and holds the divisions together. Good at focus, speed inside a domain, clear ownership, easy addition of a new division. Breaks: divisions duplicate functions and stop sharing knowledge.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Strong partial fit, best candidate for the top level. The verticals map cleanly to divisions. Borrow divisions for Worlds, but add shared infrastructure and cross-cutting links so a pattern found in one World can be seen from another.
borrowed_shapes.name: Divisional structure
borrowed_shapes.real_example: Procter and Gamble, product-based divisions (Beauty, Grooming, Health Care, Fabric and Home Care, Baby, Feminine and Family Care).

borrowed_shapes.core_idea: A stable core platform provides shared functionality and interfaces, and complementary apps or modules vary on top of it. Good at reuse of one stable core across many complements and compounding value as complements accumulate. Breaks: complementors depend on the platform owner and its rules; a core change can break many complements at once.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Strongest fit for the substrate layer, not for the whole taxonomy. The estate already has a natural core: governance, receipts and provenance, identity, search and retrieval, design system, shared infrastructure. The 500 items are natural complements. Keep the language honest: there is no external developer ecosystem here yet, only internal complements. Borrow the core versus complement distinction, the interface and standards discipline, and the rule that a core change must be checked against all complements.
borrowed_shapes.name: Platform / Ecosystem

borrowed_shapes.core_idea: Group by shared skill or function (marketing, engineering, finance, operations), one head per function. Good at deep specialization and consistent standards. Breaks: silos form, cross-functional work slows.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Weak as the primary taxonomy, useful as a secondary facet. The estate has no departments to staff; functions such as research, build, verification, distribution, and governance describe what an item does, not what it is about. Use functions as tags, not as Worlds.
borrowed_shapes.name: Functional structure
borrowed_shapes.real_example: Apple, one design team, one hardware engineering team, one software engineering team, one marketing team across all products.

borrowed_shapes.core_idea: Two axes apply at once, most often function crossed with product or project; an item sits at the intersection and is judged by both axes. Good at balancing functional depth with product focus. Breaks: dual reporting creates confusion, conflicting priorities, blurred accountability.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Useful as an indexing principle, not as a reporting structure. There are no two bosses in a one-founder codex. Borrow the matrix as a second axis only: one home World for each item, plus tags on a second axis such as lifecycle state or capability (signal, recipe, underwriting, outreach, receipt).
borrowed_shapes.name: Matrix structure
borrowed_shapes.real_example: Philips (engineers report to a functional head and a product line); Atrium Health (regional supply chain leader reports to enterprise supply chain and regional operations).

borrowed_shapes.core_idea: A parent exists mainly to own controlling interests in other companies; the parent allocates capital and selects leaders, while each subsidiary runs its own operations. Good at letting very different businesses run independently. Breaks: synergies are often promised and rarely delivered.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Partial fit for ownership and governance, poor fit as a taxonomy for artifacts. Most of the 500 items are not operating businesses. Borrow the holding idea only at the top governance layer, with an explicit test for what graduates from codex entry to real venture.
borrowed_shapes.name: Holding company / Conglomerate
borrowed_shapes.real_example: Berkshire Hathaway (GEICO, BNSF Railway, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, small Omaha headquarters focused on capital allocation).

borrowed_shapes.core_idea: Distributed nodes operate under a shared brand and a shared set of rules, while a center provides the brand, the operating system, training, and supply chain. Good at fast scaling and local adaptation. Breaks: the center loses direct control, quality depends on enforcing rules across independent operators.
borrowed_shapes.fit: Weak fit as an ownership model, narrow fit as a template pattern. There are no franchisees. Borrow only the repeatable playbook idea (one well-defined format instantiated in many places, such as a scan, dossier, demo, or paper) and the brand and rules layer that keeps public surfaces consistent.
borrowed_shapes.name: Network / Franchise
borrowed_shapes.real_example: McDonald's, over 93 percent of restaurants owned by independent franchisees.

honesty.verdict: Borrow divisional structure for the top level, platform and ecosystem for the substrate, functional structure as a tag facet, and matrix as a second index axis only. Use divisional Worlds for the verticals so each item has one clear home and one clear owner question (what domain does this help decide in). Put a platform core underneath all Worlds for governance, receipts, provenance, identity, search, and design standards, so complements reuse it instead of duplicating it. Add functional tags and a matrix-style second axis for lifecycle state and capability, so cross-vertical patterns stay findable without dual ownership. Use the holding company idea only at the governance edge, to decide what graduates to a real venture, and use the franchise idea only as a repeatable template pattern. Do not adopt any single shape wholesale; the taxonomy must stay fitted to a one-founder knowledge codex for decisions, not to a staffed company org chart.

universe.description: The sovereign-intelligence codex: one Universe, the organism substrate. Not a frontier lab and not a competitor to one. A codex of the founder's knowledge across his verticals and interests, built to work the cognitive side of a decision: take a question, run it through everything he knows, reach a conclusion he can act on.

reconciliation.note: World totals as listed sum to 1,007, counting the W04 verified subset of 15 and the W05 verified subset of 6 in place of their UNVERIFIED totals. Plus Archive layer 88, Design law layer 5, and a 3-record keyword spill (marketing records matching Real Estate/Resale keywords) equals 1,103 exactly. W04, W05, W06, W11, and W12 counts are keyword-rule carve-outs (ESTIMATE); all others are exact partition buckets.

universe.why_one: The founder's own definition in Notion Chapter 22 states the thesis as Neuruh is the substrate; Worlds are domain deployments; products are user-facing cuts. IDENTITY.md states Neuruh is best understood as a general AI execution substrate, and MEMORY.md records it as a unified organism of bounded verticals sharing infrastructure, governance, execution, and learning. No source proves a second universe. The NeuruhAI org versus the Jeramie-Hicks personal repos, the APG lineage, and the Drive estate are custody and lineage distinctions inside the one estate, not parallel universes. The Drive estate (88 records, 60 UNKNOWN) and the Notion canon (254 notion-type records) are record layers inside the Universe, not separate universes.
universe.world_creation_law: Per CH22, a new World should be existing organ composition plus domain contracts plus source adapters plus evaluation pack plus policy overlay plus projection. Not new database plus new router plus new governance plus new memory plus new receipt format.
universe.premise: This is NOT a frontier lab and NOT a competitor to one. It is a codex of Jeramie's knowledge across his verticals and interests, built to work the cognitive side of a decision: take a question, run it through everything he knows, reach a conclusion he can act on. Structure is universes, then worlds, then planets, then granular detail, like a business org chart where marketing is not with the mechanics. The end state is sovereign intelligence he can build anything off of, not an operating system.
